newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jail sought for two French surgeons.
newsitem.headline: Jail sought for two French surgeons.

text.p: A prosecutor asked a French court on Friday to jail two surgeons accused of performing unnecessary operations on patients in order to increase their clinic's financial turnover.

State prosecutor Herve Robin said the surgeons regarded the people they treated as clients rather than patients. He asked the court to jail urologist Georges Rossignol for five to seven years and colleague Pierre Leandri for one year.
Experts told the court the surgeons removed the bladder or prostate of patients diagnosed with cancer rather than resort to less drastic threatments.
One patient said his wife left him after an operation, later deemed unnecessary, left him incontinent and impotent.

The surgeons, who had an international reputation, argue that, if mistakes were made, they were involuntary errors of diagnosis. They are charged with wilfully causing bodily harm leading to mutilation or permanent disability.
Presiding judge Jean Boyer said they had committed themselves to a minimum turnover in order to buy shares in the private clinic where they worked.
The court in the southwestern town of Toulouse is to rule in the case on February 24.
